E1 describes ductility loss at intermediate temperatures (400–800°C) due to a different mechanism, E2 is truncated but discusses UHV sliding and low friction without establishing grain refinement or inverse Hall-Petch, and E3 mentions grain-boundary decohesion without segregation but does not link it to dynamic grain refinement or cavitation under high strain rates. The core mechanistic chain is unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: High strain-rate deformation induces extreme grain refinement at high-angle grain boundaries in single-phase HEAs
This refinement suppresses dislocation plasticity via an inverse Hall-Petch effect
Localized grain-boundary sliding then concentrates stress and promotes microvoid formation (cavitation) and decohesion
This dynamic process leads to brittle failure independent of impurity segregation or intermetallic precipitation
The mechanism operates at low-to-moderate temperatures under chemically inert conditions where thermal diffusion is minimal
